hero.subtitle: A fall at a Loma Linda store, medical facility, or apartment complex can leave you with injuries and unanswered questions about who's responsible. We can help you understand your options and handle your premises liability claim in San Bernardino County at no upfront cost to you.

about.title: Loma Linda Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Loma Linda's mix of medical campuses, retail centers along Redlands Boulevard, and residential complexes near Mountain View Avenue means falls happen in a variety of settings — hospital lobbies, grocery aisles, parking lots, and stairwells. Under California law, an injured person generally has to show the property owner or manager knew, or reasonably should have known, about a hazardous condition and didn't fix it or warn visitors in time. That's why what happens right after a fall matters. Photos of the spill, debris, or broken step; the names of any witnesses; and a request to preserve surveillance footage can all become important later. Our team handles premises liability claims in Loma Linda and can evaluate the notice element, gather evidence before it disappears, and work on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless money is recovered.
about.ctaText: Tell us what happened — contact us for your free case review.

whyChoose.title: Why Loma Linda Residents Choose Us

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California premises liability claims hinge on proving the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. We can help pin down how long a spill, crack, or debris was left unaddressed.

items.title: Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to send a preservation request can protect evidence that might otherwise be lost.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly blamed for not seeing a hazard, you may still recover a reduced amount. We can help present your side clearly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Loma Linda?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity — for example, a government building or facility — the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim filing, so it's worth having a review done sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I fell at a Loma Linda medical facility or hospital campus?
items.answer: Falls at healthcare campuses raise the same notice question as any other property: did the facility know about the hazard, such as a wet floor or uneven walkway, and fail to address it? We can look into maintenance records and staff logs to help answer that.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. There's no charge for an initial consultation, and we typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with us.
